what: Finding 1: final-bail-reason persistence is planned at a lifecycle point that the new bail path will miss
scenario_or_breakage: The FIX_ATTEMPTS>=10 path sets BAIL_REASON and exits 3 before postmerge; final-bail-reason.txt is only restored in Step 18, after refresh-run-logs has already run and with no subsequent larch-log commit/push, so the committed final-bail-reason batch remains absent on the path this PR is trying to diagnose
suggested_fix: Write the batch at a terminal bail lifecycle point that actually runs after BAIL_REASON exists, such as immediately before exit 3/4 or in Step 18 after restore-finalize-state and before cleanup, and define the commit/push behavior needed for it to reach the committed run log

what: Finding 2: the plan does not test the real ci-decide producer for the new magic token
scenario_or_breakage: The existing ship-pr exit-3 test injects STUB_BAIL_REASON=fix-attempts-exhausted directly through the ci-wait stub, so a typo or regression in ci-decide.sh at the FIX_ATTEMPTS cap would still leave the planned tests green while exit 3 remains unreachable in production
suggested_fix: Add a producer-level regression, either a direct ci-decide cap test or a ci-wait test using the real ci-decide.sh, asserting --fix-attempts 10 emits BAIL_REASON=fix-attempts-exhausted and routes to ship-pr exit 3

what: Finding 3: the plan adds a committed run-log batch but omits the canonical run-log batch reference
scenario_or_breakage: docs/run-logs.md is the consumer-facing batch file reference and directory projection; after adding final-bail-reason.txt, consumers and completeness tooling documentation will not describe the new artifact or when it is written
suggested_fix: Update docs/run-logs.md to include final-bail-reason.txt in the tree and add a short batch section covering mode, write lifecycle, and absence conditions
